title: Access Patient Transport Service (PTS)
summary: Find out if you can access the Patient Transport Service (PTS) for transport to or from a health facility.
intro:
If you need transport to or from a health facility such as a hospital or rehabilitation unit, you may be able to access the Patient Transport Service. The service is offered to patients who don't require emergency ambulance services and is provided by NSW Health.

To be eligible you need to be:

Only health professionals and staff in hospitals, aged care facilities, private hospitals, nursing homes and general practitioner's surgeries can make bookings.

For information about this service, including eligibility requirements and instructions on how to book, visit NSW Health.
who_can_apply: Must be a patient who does not require emergency ambulance services.
Bookings must be made by health professionals and staff in hospitals, aged care facilities, private hospitals, nursing homes, or general practitioner's surgeries.

faqs.q: Who is the Patient Transport Service (PTS) for?
faqs.a: The service provides transport to or from a health facility, such as a hospital or rehabilitation unit, for patients who do not require emergency ambulance services.

faqs.q: Who can book the Patient Transport Service?
faqs.a: Only health professionals and staff in hospitals, aged care facilities, private hospitals, nursing homes, and general practitioner's surgeries can make bookings.

faqs.q: Where can I find more information about this service?
faqs.a: For detailed information, including eligibility requirements and booking instructions, visit NSW Health.
